findings.finding: Detector v2 analyzes only one selected keyframe per video.
Using all existing OpenCV keyframes raises temporal coverage without changing sampling.
All four intervals not covered by existing keyframes were nevertheless captured by the 1 Hz sampler.
Motion-dependent defects such as water leaks and dripping faucets may not be visible in one still frame.
Static visible defects can still be missed by the vision models.

detector_v3_design_direction: Replace the one-keyframe-per-video policy with multi-keyframe temporal coverage.
Reuse the existing 1 Hz sampler initially; do not increase sampling frequency yet.
Preserve selected keyframes across the video rather than collapsing them to one frame.
Rescue useful rejected samples when temporal gaps would otherwise remain, including frames rejected as duplicates, low marginal value, or fast camera motion.
Use short multi-frame temporal evidence for motion-dependent defects such as leaks and dripping faucets.
Improve static-defect recognition for cracked glass, weathering, moisture damage and deterioration.
Protect Detector v2's zero-clean-false-positive baseline while increasing recall.
next_step: Step 42B — implement and evaluate the first Detector v3 temporal-coverage candidate before changing the 1 Hz sampler.
